levels.target: Aim to move from below 50% towards a safe pass band by writing complete, keyword-bearing answers to the easier 1-mark and 2-mark questions across all three subjects.
signs: Biology: diagrams drawn without labels, key terms missing, and definitions written loosely in the student's own words
Chemistry and Physics: bare final answers with no formula, no steps and no unit; sign errors in numericals
Case-based and assertion-reason questions attempted without reading the passage or the reason carefully; several parts left blank
first: Learn the NCERT definitions and keyword lists for Biology line by line and write each one out from memory
Practise 2-mark and 3-mark numericals in full format: formula, substitution, answer, unit
Redraw and label 10 core Biology diagrams (flower, embryo sac, lac operon, replication fork) until every label is automatic
Attempt every question; write at least the formula or the first correct step

levels.target: Aim for the 65 to 80% band by removing the avoidable deductions: missing keywords, missing units and half-written steps.
signs: Biology: the idea is right but one or two NCERT keywords are missing, so a mark is lost in each 3-mark answer
Chemistry and Physics: correct method but small slips such as a wrong factor n, a forgotten unit or a skipped substitution
Case-based questions answered from memory of the chapter instead of from the passage given
first: Make a keyword sheet per Biology chapter and check each written answer against it
Write every numerical in four lines: formula, substitution, answer, unit
Do timed Section C practice (3 marks in about 5 minutes) and self-mark in the CBSE style
Read case-based passages twice and underline the data you will quote
later: Rare exceptions and fine-print NCERT exemplar problems
Speed practice beyond the paper-length target

levels.target: Aim to move from the 65 to 80% band towards 80%+ by closing the last half-marks: precise terms, full diagrams and clean steps.
signs: Biology: answers are correct but a diagram label, a term such as 'triploid' or 'operator', or a one-line consequence is occasionally left out
Chemistry and Physics: correct working but the final unit, a sign convention statement or a nature-of-image remark is dropped
Time spent unevenly, so the last long-answer questions are written in a rush
first: Audit your last three mock papers, list every half-mark lost and group them by type
Add a closing line to each Biology answer that names the product or consequence in NCERT words
State the sign convention or the law used before every numerical
Practise competency-based questions that mix two chapters
later: Rewriting answers that already score full marks
Collecting extra reference books before the NCERT is mastered

levels.target: Aim to hold 80% and above under exam pressure and keep the same answer-writing discipline for NEET-style speed and accuracy.
signs: Biology: neatly labelled diagrams, every NCERT keyword present and answers within the mark allotment

sheets.subject: Biology
sheets.q: Explain the events of double fertilisation in an angiosperm. Name the structures formed from the products of the two fusions.

scheme.point: Pollen tube enters the embryo sac and discharges two male gametes
Syngamy: one male gamete fuses with the egg to form the diploid zygote, which develops into the embryo
Triple fusion: the other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN), which develops into the endosperm

lines: The pollen tube goes to the ovule.
One makes the seed and one makes the food.
sheets.note: Only the idea of two fusions is hinted at. No male gametes, zygote, polar nuclei or PEN are named. Partial credit of 0.5 is given under point 1 for the pollen tube reaching the ovule.

lines: The pollen tube enters the embryo sac and releases two male gametes.
One male gamete fuses with the egg and forms the diploid zygote, which becomes the embryo.
The other male gamete fuses with the polar nuclei and forms the endosperm.
sheets.note: The first two points are complete. In the third, the fusion is described only as with 'the polar nuclei': the number (two), the term triple fusion and the triploid PEN are missing, so the mark is withheld. Awarded 1 + 1 + 0.

lines: The pollen tube enters the embryo sac and discharges two male gametes.
Syngamy: one male gamete fuses with the egg to form the diploid zygote, which develops into the embryo.
Triple fusion: the other male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei to form the triploid primary endosperm nucleus (PEN).
The PEN develops into the endosperm. Both fusions together are called double fertilisation.
sheets.note: All three value points are present with the correct keywords: syngamy, triple fusion, diploid, triploid, PEN and endosperm. Awarded 1 + 1 + 1.

sheets.tip: Name the ploidy and the end product of each fusion; these keywords carry the marks.

sheets.subject: Biology
sheets.q: Describe the working of the lac operon when lactose is absent in the medium. Name the genes involved and the enzymes whose production is stopped.

scheme.point: The regulatory i gene makes the repressor protein (all the time, i.e. constitutively)
The repressor binds to the operator and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the structural genes
Structural genes z, y, a are not transcribed, so beta-galactosidase, permease and transacetylase are not made

lines: Lac operon is a group of genes.
When there is no lactose it is switched off.
sheets.note: Says only switched off. The repressor, operator and the three structural genes are missing. Partial credit of 0.5 under point 3 for the idea that enzymes are not made.

lines: The i gene makes the repressor protein.
The repressor binds to the operator.
So RNA polymerase cannot work and the enzymes are not made.
sheets.note: Points 1 and 2 are correct in substance. The last line does not name z, y, a or any enzyme, and does not say transcription of the structural genes is blocked. Awarded 1 + 1 + 0.

lines: The regulatory i gene continuously makes the repressor protein.
With no lactose (inducer), the repressor binds to the operator and prevents RNA polymerase from transcribing the operon.
RNA polymerase cannot transcribe the structural genes z, y and a.
So beta-galactosidase, permease and transacetylase are not produced.
sheets.note: Complete: i gene, repressor, operator, z-y-a and all three enzymes named. Awarded 1 + 1 + 1.

sheets.tip: Always link the chain: regulator gene, repressor, operator, then which structural genes stay off.

sheets.subject: Chemistry
sheets.q: Liquids A and B form an ideal solution at a given temperature. The vapour pressure of pure A is 300 mm Hg and of pure B is 500 mm Hg. A solution is made from 1 mol of A and 3 mol of B. Calculate the total vapour pressure of the solution.

scheme.point: Raoult's law: pA = xA pA0 = 75 mm Hg and pB = xB pB0 = 375 mm Hg
Total pressure P = pA + pB = 450 mm Hg (with unit)

sheets.note: Adds the pure vapour pressures without using mole fractions, so Raoult's law is not applied and the answer is wrong. No value point is earned.
Mole fractions and partial pressures are correct (2 marks). The final answer has no unit mm Hg and Raoult's law is not stated, so the last mark is lost.

lines: By Raoult's law, pA = xA pA0 = 0.25 x 300 = 75 mm Hg
pB = xB pB0 = 0.75 x 500 = 375 mm Hg
sheets.note: Law stated, each step shown, final answer with unit. Awarded 1 + 1 + 1.

sheets.tip: Find mole fractions first, then partial pressures, then add; write the unit.

sheets.subject: Chemistry
sheets.q: Calculate the emf of the cell Zn | Zn2+ (0.01 M) || Cu2+ (1 M) | Cu at 298 K. Given E0(Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V, E0(Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V. Use 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V.

scheme.point: Nernst equation with n = 2: E = E0 - (0.059/2) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+])
Substitution and answer: E = 1.10 + 0.059 = 1.159 V (about 1.16 V)

sheets.note: The standard emf earns 1 mark. The concentration given in the question is ignored, so the Nernst equation and the final value 1.159 V are missing.

E0cell is correct (1). The Nernst equation has the right form and Q but n = 1 instead of 2 (0.5). The substitution and log value are correct, but the final 1.218 V is wrong because of n (0.5). Total 2.

lines: Zn + Cu2+ -> Zn2+ + Cu, so n = 2
sheets.note: Correct E0cell, correct n = 2 and Q, correct arithmetic. Awarded 1 + 1 + 1.

sheets.tip: Count the electrons from the balanced reaction before writing the Nernst equation.

sheets.subject: Physics
sheets.q: A convex lens has a focal length of 20 cm. An object is placed 30 cm from the lens. Find the position, nature and magnification of the image.

scheme.point: Lens formula 1/v - 1/u = 1/f with the sign convention (u = -30 cm, f = +20 cm)
v = +60 cm, on the other side of the lens
m = v/u = -2; the image is real, inverted and magnified

sheets.note: Gives a value with no formula or sign convention; u was taken as positive, so v is wrong. Partial credit of 0.5 under point 3 for the correct statement that the image is real.
Formula with convention and v with unit are correct (2 marks). m = -2 is found but the nature of the image (real, inverted, magnified) is not stated, so the last mark is lost. Awarded 1 + 1 + 0.

lines: Using 1/v - 1/u = 1/f with u = -30 cm and f = +20 cm
1/v = 1/20 - 1/30 = 1/60, so v = +60 cm (on the other side of the lens)
The image is real, inverted and twice the size of the object.
sheets.note: Convention stated, correct v with unit, correct m and nature. Awarded 1 + 1 + 1.

sheets.tip: Write the sign convention and the nature of the image to secure the last mark.

sheets.subject: Physics
sheets.q: A point charge of 4 microcoulomb is placed at the centre of a cube. Using Gauss's law, find the electric flux through the whole cube and through each face. Take epsilon0 = 8.85 x 10^-12 C^2 N^-1 m^-2.

scheme.point: Flux through each face = total/6 = 7.5 x 10^4 N m^2 C^-1 (7.53 x 10^4 also accepted), by symmetry

sheets.note: The law is recalled (1 mark). The charge 4 microcoulomb is not converted to 4 x 10^-6 C, so the total flux is wrong by 10^6; the unit and the flux through one face are missing. Awarded 1 + 0 + 0.
The law and the total flux with unit are correct (2 marks). The face value is divided by 6 without the symmetry reason and without the unit, so the last mark is lost. Awarded 1 + 1 + 0.

lines: The charge is at the centre, so by symmetry each of the 6 faces gets equal flux.
Flux per face = 4.52 x 10^5 / 6 = 7.5 x 10^4 N m^2 C^-1
sheets.note: Law, substitution, symmetry reason and units all present. Awarded 1 + 1 + 1.

sheets.tip: The charge at the centre means equal flux through each face: say it, then divide by 6.
